A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MHRoPE and MRoPE-I research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite added experiments and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, positional-design and frequency-allocation ablations, attention analyses, and long-context experiments in Section 3 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds BLINK evaluation, Qwen3-VL experiments, a controlled YaRN comparison, and additional allocation-ratio ablations.

M1.justification: Both versions propose the same spatial-reset mechanism, head-based frequency allocation in MHRoPE, and interleaved allocation in MRoPE-I. Additional backbone evaluations and YaRN tests do not revise the proposed methods; YaRN compatibility was already described in v1.

E1.justification: v3 adds BLINK for dedicated multi-image reasoning evaluation, a focused extension of the retained image, video, and grounding coverage. Multi-turn dialogue is also newly listed within the approximately 2M training samples, but the PDFs do not establish that the training corpus itself changed.

E2.justification: The main comparisons retain vanilla RoPE, MRoPE, VideoRoPE, HoPE, and CircleRoPE. Appendix D.3 newly evaluates MRoPE with YaRN against MRoPE-I with YaRN and their unscaled controls in Table 6; v1 instead discussed scaling relative to vanilla RoPE.

E3.justification: Section 3.3 and Appendix D.6 extend evaluation beyond the original Qwen2.5 7B setup to Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct and Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, testing materially different model configurations. New experiments introduce controlled YaRN comparisons at 256K and additional frequency-allocation settings. Newly specified optimizer and preprocessing details for existing experiments are disclosures, not established changes to those experiments.

E4.justification: v3 adds architectural portability tests, directly tests YaRN compatibility through with/without comparisons on LVBench and MLVU, and expands allocation sensitivity to 0:32:32 and 12:26:26, including removal of temporal channels. These substantially extend the questions examined. Existing position-design, attention, temporal-stride, and long-context analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The additional experiments retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v3 adds BLINK scores, complete Qwen3-VL results, YaRN results, and two allocation-ratio rows. For example, Table 6 reports MRoPE-I LVBench scores of 42.0 without YaRN and 43.6 with YaRN at 256K. Existing individual Table 2 benchmark scores remain unchanged, but MHRoPE's video average changes from 52.98 to 52.58, placing HoPE first, and HoPE's grounding average changes from 73.19 to 73.34. Image aggregates change with BLINK included and are not same-coverage performance losses. The earlier three-quarter YaRN scaling observation is removed.

T1.justification: The RoPE definitions, relative-position equations, and Appendix D.2 attention-bound derivation are unchanged in substance. Equation 4 only gains a prime on the relative-position variable. Appendix D.3 replaces explanatory and empirical scaling discussion without changing the underlying indexing rules or formal derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: systematic analysis, three design guidelines, MHRoPE and MRoPE-I, and spatial-reset. Additional evaluations support these retained claims rather than redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 introduces an architectural-generalization rationale based on common LLM backbones and interprets Qwen3-VL results as evidence of robustness. Appendix D.3 replaces the smaller-required-scaling explanation with an interpretation that MRoPE-I benefits more from YaRN than MRoPE. Existing failure-mode explanations and MHRoPE versus MRoPE-I tradeoffs remain.

D1.justification: Section 3.1 substantially expands reproducibility information: AdamW parameters 0.9/0.98, weight decay 0.05, minimum learning rate 3e-6, a 24K visual-token cap, smart resizing, and 2 FPS sampling with a 768-frame fallback. Section 2.2.3 also discloses the duplicated-image prompt used for Figure 2. The abstract changes promised code release to claimed availability, although Appendix B retains future-release wording. Appendix D.3 removes the previous three-quarter YaRN scaling guidance.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to BLINK, Qwen3-VL, Apollo, and Cambrian-1. Section 3.1 newly positions its initialization alongside VideoRoPE and HoPE and distinguishes it from Apollo and Cambrian-1. The broader positioning against earlier positional encodings remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the overall narrative are retained. Local changes expand experimental setup, add Section 3.3 and Appendix D.6, rewrite part of Appendix D.3, and clarify Figure 2's setup. Headers change from under review to published, with corresponding section and table renumbering.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the table presentation through the Qwen3-VL summary and detailed Tables 3, 10, and 11, plus YaRN Table 6. Table 2 adds BLINK and removes colored parenthetical gains; the allocation-ratio table gains two rows. Figure 1(e) is redrawn. The remaining figures and existing ablation displays are largely retained.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens empirical support through multi-image, architectural-portability, and controlled YaRN tests, while added implementation details and corrected aggregates improve reproducibility and accuracy. The gains remain limited: architectural validation stays within Qwen, the new claim of consistently best performance overstates Table 3(b)'s video results, and earlier YaRN scaling guidance is removed. These tradeoffs leave a clear but modest net improvement.
